picks.style: highland bardic lament, clarsach harp, low bowed drone, weathered male voice, slow, misty, elegiac
picks.why: Autumn dark on the mountains, a lone tree marking a grave — the whole passage is one sustained elegy, image after image.

picks.style: ossianic dirge, solo clarsach, sparse bowed strings, aged male voice, very slow, desolate, sea-wind
picks.why: Ossian outliving every other bard: 'my voice remains, like a blast, that roars, lonely, on a sea-surrounded rock.'

picks.style: gaelic pastoral duet, clarsach and low whistle, male and female voices answering, tender, unhurried, windswept
picks.why: Vinvela and Shilric answering each other across the hill — a natural two-voice song, 'bright as the bow of heaven; as the moon on the western wave.'

picks.style: roman hexameter chant, kithara, low sustained strings, measured male voice, stately, cosmological
picks.why: 'What, on earth and in heaven, remains without the law of obeying?' — stars, moon, kings and Rome all bound in one turning order.

picks.style: latin funeral lament, double tibia pipes, muffled frame drum, grieving male voice, slow, raw, unresolved
picks.why: A consolation that admits it cannot console: the wound still gaping, the mourner turning a deaf ear to the lyre.

picks.style: roman convivial song, lyre, tambourine, light tenor, playful, quick, festive
picks.why: 'Pour the cups, boy—but do not labour to count them' — Statius dismissing the Muses for a friend's bath-house, wholly buoyant.

picks.style: georgian moral ode, harpsichord, chamber strings, clear baritone, measured, wry
picks.why: 'Complain that life affords but little joy, / And yet that little foolishly destroy' — a whole argument about self-made misery, epigram by epigram.

picks.style: late baroque air, viola da gamba, harpsichord continuo, dark baritone, slow, bitter
picks.why: 'I thought men worthless, now I've prov'd 'em so' — cold anatomy of mankind closing on wisdom bought too dear.

picks.style: 18th century english art song, fortepiano, plaintive soprano, yearning, rubato, intimate
picks.why: 'Acceptance is the heav'n which mortals know, / But 'tis the bliss of angels to bestow' — the Ovidian complaint turning into a real theology of giving.

picks.style: english cathedral hymn, organ and strings, boy treble with choir, bright, processional, ecstatic
picks.why: Song to David's adoration stanzas — crocus, pheasant, holly, squirrel, all held by the repeating word ADORATION; a built-in refrain.

picks.style: anthem for choir and organ, full choir, brass, exultant, rising, jubilant
picks.why: 'God's harp thy symbol, and thy type / The lion and the bee!' — Smart at his strangest and most triumphant.

picks.style: pastoral sacred blank verse, chamber organ, flute, warm tenor, unhurried, birdsong-lit
picks.why: Blackbird, thrush and even the harsh ravens meaning their noise for praise, 'and leave ingratitude to man.'

picks.style: georgian comic ballad, fiddle, harpsichord continuo, arch tenor patter, brisk, satirical
picks.why: Jotham's fable turned election farce — olive, fig and vine all refuse the crown, and the mob cries 'a bramble! a bramble!'

picks.style: mock-oriental comic air, plucked strings, bassoon, sly baritone, jaunty, deadpan
picks.why: The holy man who becomes the oracle of his nation purely by running long nails into his backside — the satire lands in the first breath.

picks.style: mock-elegy drawing room song, harpsichord, muted strings, arch soprano, feigned pathos, gently comic
picks.why: 'To me alone no card is come, / I must not go abroad — and cannot be at home' — high elegiac machinery cranked up for an unsent invitation.

picks.style: elizabethan pastoral pastiche, lute, recorder, gentle tenor, flowing, sunlit, archaic diction
picks.why: The great sheltering oak with its bees, acorns and safe birds' nests — a complete idyll before the fall.

picks.style: tudor ballad, lute and tabor, stern baritone, building from hush to thunder, archaic
picks.why: The axe answers the oak's hospitality, and Jove replies in thunder: 'On high Olympus next mine tree I'll place.'

picks.style: ancient greek martial declamation, aulos, kithara, frame drum, strong male voice, rising, warlike
picks.why: Fortune's claim on Alexander refuted by his own wounds, ending on the Spartan tag that the well-tuned lyre unsheathes the sword.

picks.style: medieval plainchant, unaccompanied male schola, latinate monody, very slow, solemn, stone-reverberant
picks.why: Only candidate in the work: a king's epitaph, and its bare recital of kalends and indictions carries as chant.
